hints: Work out the product with two factors, then three.
Small cases reveal a pattern for the product up to n. Then confirm it by factoring each term as a difference of squares, which makes neighbouring factors cancel.
1 - 1/k^2 = ((k - 1)/k) x ((k + 1)/k). Up to 2 the product is 3/4, up to 3 it is 2/3 = 4/6, up to 4 it is 5/8.

solutions.reliable: Small cases: up to 2, 3/4; up to 3, 3/4 x 8/9 = 2/3 = 4/6; up to 4, 2/3 x 15/16 = 5/8. The pattern is (n + 1)/(2n). To confirm, write 1 - 1/k^2 = ((k - 1)/k)((k + 1)/k). The (k - 1)/k parts multiply to 1/n and the (k + 1)/k parts multiply to (n + 1)/2. For n = 10 the product is 11/20. The transferable idea: compute two or three small cases to see the pattern, then justify it with a telescoping factorisation.
solutions.elegant: Each factor splits into a part that telescopes down to 1/10 and a part that telescopes up to 11/2, so the product is 11/20.

whyOnTest: Long products and sums test whether you try small cases, see the cancelling pattern, and use the right value of n at the end.
